--- order: 7 unit: challenge assumes: [js-event, text-content, create-element, append-element, class-list] title: "Final challenge: a quiz page" summary: "Put it all together: a list of questions as data, buttons made for each choice, a score that remembers, and feedback on every click." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 6 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: "A quiz is a click, a check and some feedback" clip: - caption: "A question, two answer buttons, and a place for the result." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "

What is 3 + 4?

\n\n\n

\n", append: true} - caption: "One function checks an answer: an if decides what to say." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 400 - click: {selector: "#a1", preview: true} - expect: {selector: "#result", contains: "Try again", preview: true} - caption: "The wrong answer says try again." - click: {selector: "#a2", preview: true} - expect: {selector: "#result", contains: "Correct!", preview: true} - caption: text: "The right one says Correct. The challenge does this for a whole list of questions." say: "The right one says Correct. The challenge asks a whole list." hook: "By the end you'll have a real quiz on one page: questions, a score and feedback on every click." --- Your quiz keeps its questions as **data**, in an array of objects, and uses everything from the course: - an **array of objects** holds the questions (`questions[current].text`), - **`createElement`** makes a button for each choice, - **click handlers** check the answer, - **variables** above the handlers keep `current` (which question) and `score`, - an **`if`** decides what to say, and another decides when the quiz is over. **The hard part** is keeping track of what changes. Only two variables change: `current` and `score`. Everything on the page is a picture of them and of `questions[current]`. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict check: type: predict q: "A student clicks 6, then clicks 7. What does the result say at the end?" options: ["Correct!", "Try again", "Correct! Try again", "Nothing: the result is empty"] actual: "Correct! Each click runs pick and sets the result. The second click replaces the first message: textContent replaces the words." ``` Does the second click add to the first message, or replace it? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I played the quiz through and saw the score and the final message." } ``` Play the quiz: three questions, a score and a message at the end. The questions are an **array of objects** at the top; the rest of the page is built from them. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "The quiz is data plus two variables: the array of questions, the number of the current question, and the score; each click checks one answer, changes the variables, then shows the next question." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each piece with what it does." pairs: - ["questions[current].answer", "the right answer shown now"] - ["for (const c of q.choices) { … }", "makes one button for each choice"] - ["current = current + 1;", "moves on to the next question"] - ["if (current < questions.length) { … } else { … }", "next question or the end"] - check: type: question q: "You want to add a fourth question. What is the smallest change?" options: ["Add one more object to the questions array", "Add a new function", "Add a new button in the HTML", "Change the score"] answer: 0 explain: "The page is built from the array. One more object gives one more question, with its own choices and answer: nothing else needs to change." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "Every answer says Correct!, even the wrong ones. There is no red error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 27 fault: logic misconception: assign-in-if explain: "One = puts the answer into choice and is always true. Compare with three: choice === questions[current].answer." ``` ### Which piece does what? Data, buttons, memory and decisions. ### A fourth question Where the data lives. ### Spot the bug Every answer is right. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Feedback can be shown with a colour, and the end message can say how many were right out of how many." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } tasks: - hint: - "The feedback line is a paragraph like any other. What can you change about it?" - "Inside each branch, set feedbackEl.style.color: green when correct, crimson when not." expected: page.html#sol-colour check: { type: code, text: "Show the feedback in green when right and crimson when wrong.", rules: { contains: [".style.color"] } } - hint: - "The end message is built by joining pieces of text." - "Join \"You scored \", the score, \" of \" and questions.length." expected: page.html#sol-total try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#sol-colour", height: 430 } check: { type: code, text: "Finish with You scored 2 of 3 instead of Score: 2.", rules: { contains: ["questions.length", "scored"] } } ``` ### Colours Right is green, wrong is red. ### Out of three Use the length of the array. ## Make: your own quiz ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: a quiz on a topic you know, with at least five questions, a score, feedback, and a Play again button." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I made a quiz on a topic I know, with at least five questions, a score, feedback and a Play again button. A friend played it and I changed one thing." } ``` Make your own quiz on a topic you know well, with at least **five questions**, a **score**, **feedback** on every answer, and a **Play again** button. Then ask a friend to play it, watch what they do, and change one thing. The page on this lesson is a space quiz. Large projects, such as many quizzes or a timer, belong in your own time. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "A bigger version of your quiz saves the best score for next time. What would it need that this page does not have?" options: ["A way to store data between visits, such as a server or the browser's own storage", "A longer array", "More buttons", "A second script"] answer: 0 explain: "A page forgets everything when it is closed. Remembering between visits needs somewhere to keep data: in the browser, or on a server, as in the Python web apps course." ``` **Challenge complete** when the three required checks are done. From here: the real browser console (optional), a bigger project of your own, or the Python web apps course for pages that remember. ```teacher summary: Students build and extend a quiz page from an array of questions, buttons made for each choice, click handlers, a score and a question number, fix an answer check that is always true, add colour feedback and a total, and make a quiz of their own. time: 65 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 15 min · Make 25 min goals: - I can build a page that reacts to clicks with data from an array. - I can keep a score and a question number in variables. - I can make a quiz of my own and test it with someone. before: > Read the unit primer first. This is the final challenge; it marks "Challenge complete". It mirrors the p5.js and Python challenges: a list of data, a loop, a handler, a score. Everything has been taught; the new part is putting it together. The questions are an array of objects, buttons are made from the choices, `check(choice)` is the handler, `current` and `score` are the only variables that change. The bug is a single `=` in an `if`: no error, every answer is right; the p5 course had `>` where `<` belonged. Quizzes that save results or send them anywhere are out of scope: the playground sends nothing. Large projects belong to the teacher (a unit project, a class quiz bank). running: - "Predict: ask what the page says after each click." - "Run: let students play and call out scores." - 'Investigate: for the bug, ask "does one = compare, or put?"' - "Modify: ask which two variables change when a question is answered." - "Make: pairs write their questions on paper first; swap and play before changing." stuck: - see: Every answer is correct. ask: Does the check use ===? fix: Compare with three equal signs. - see: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading text). ask: Has current gone past the end of the array? fix: Stop at questions.length before showing the next question. - see: The buttons pile up. ask: Is the old choices box emptied first? fix: Set choicesEl.textContent = "" before making new buttons. - see: The score is wrong after Play again. ask: Was the score set back to 0? fix: Reset current, score and the text on the page. stretch: Shuffle the questions, add a timer with setInterval, or give harder questions more points using a property on each object. support: Give the whole quiz and ask students to add only questions of their own, then the colour feedback. leads: "Optional next lesson: the real browser console. Beyond the course: the Python web apps course, to keep results between visits." exit: q: Which two variables change as the quiz is played? a: current, the number of the question on the screen, and score, how many were right. explain: | 1. The questions are an array of objects: text, choices and answer. 2. Buttons are made for each choice; a click calls `check`. 3. `current` and `score` are the only memory; the page shows them. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-colour step-4#t2: page.html#sol-total step-5: page.html#sol-make struggle: "Where the data lives: the page is built from the array, and only current and score change. Draw those two boxes on the board." ```
